prompt_text: What is the best tool for an Airbnb host to set nightly pricing and analyze a market before buying?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: use two tools together — AirDNA (or Mashvisor/AllTheRooms) to analyze a market before you buy, and a dynamic-pricing tool (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse or Beyond Pricing) to set nightly rates once you have a listing. For most hosts the best combo is AirDNA for market research + PriceLabs for pricing automation.

Why this combo
- AirDNA (MarketMinder) — best-in-class market-level analytics: historical ADR, occupancy, seasonality, revenue estimates, comps by property type and neighborhood, supply growth, and demand windows. It lets you estimate expected revenue, cash-on-cash return and cap rate before purchasing.
- PriceLabs — very flexible, powerful dynamic pricing engine with granular rules, minimum/maximums, length-of-stay, last-minute boosts, and broad integrations (Airbnb, Vrbo, channel managers). It’s widely used by individual hosts and property managers.
- Alternatives: Wheelhouse (great insights + easy UI), Beyond Pricing (very hands-off, good for hosts who want set-and-forget), Mashvisor or AllTheRooms for lower-cost or complementary market data, and Transparent for enterprise-level analytics.

What to look for when choosing
- Coverage for your exact city/neighborhood (some tools are stronger in major markets)
- Data you need for buy/no-buy: ADR, occupancy trends, seasonality, revenue per available rental night, comps, new listings pipeline
- Integrations (Airbnb, Vrbo, PMS/channel manager)
- Customization: ability to set rules, minimum stays, weekends, event pricing
- Trial period and pricing model (flat monthly vs percent of revenue)
- Ease of use vs control (Beyond Pricing more automated; PriceLabs more customizable)

How to use them (quick workflow)
1. Pre-purchase market research: run the target zip/neighborhood in AirDNA (or Mashvisor) -> check ADR, occupancy, revenue, seasonality, top comps, and supply trends -> run revenue and ROI scenarios for your planned property (furnished vs unfurnished, occupancy assumptions).
2. After you buy/list: connect your listing to a pricing tool (PriceLabs/Wheelhouse/Beyond Pricing) -> set base price and your rules (min nights, cleaning fees excluded from dynamic price, discounts for long stays) -> review suggestions and make manual tweaks for local events/unique features -> monitor performance and adjust.

If you tell me the city/neighborhood and the type of property you’re considering (studio/1BR/entire home) I can run a quick, actionable checklist of what metrics to evaluate and which tool would be best for that market.
